To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
residual melanoma was only found in four (0.5 %) out of 812 initially completely excised Dutch melanomas and that the re-excision of completely excised primary melanomas may not be cost-effective.
in <1 % (4 out of 812) of initially completely excisional melanomas, residual tumour was found in the subsequent re-excision specimen.
in <1 % (4 of 812) of completely excised thin melanomas, residual disease was found in the corresponding re-excision specimen, which was not associated with a worse prognosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the current recommendation of the Dutch Melanoma Guideline for re-excision of a completely excised melanoma is still valid.
the question how many melanoma cases with a completely excised primary tumor need to be re-excised in practice.
the question whether histopathological examination is required of the re-exision scar of completely excised thin melanomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
histopathological examination is not needed in the majority of re-excision scars after a completely excised melanoma.
histopathological examination is not mandatory for re-excision specimens, but may be considered in case of doubt.
in case of a primary excision without residual melanoma, a re-excision specimen may be omitted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Dutch melanoma guideline is correct.
in case of a completely excised melanoma with a free margin of >1.5 mm, a re-excision may be safely omitted.
in case of complete excision of a melanoma, a re-excision is only indicated in case of a narrow margin of <1 mm, or when a melanoma in situ is present in the margin of the primary excision.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current Dutch recommendation for histopathological evaluation of re-excision scar specimens of initially completely excision melanomas may be reconsidered and that a more cost-effective approach may be feasible.
in a large series of melanomas with a completely excised primary, only 0.5 % had residual disease in the re-exision specimen.
a histopathological examination should be done on the scar tissue of the re-excised site, and not on a random block of the reexcised specimen.   1.
